newsitem.title: UK: Carlton says outlook good for ad revenue.
newsitem.headline: Carlton says outlook good for ad revenue.

text.p: Carlton Communications Plc said on Wednesday that it was optimistic about the television advertising market following a flat performance in 1996.

"The outlook for advertising revenue is good as optimism about the economy continues to grow," managing director June de Moller said in a statement. Carlton's Television division reported a five percent increase in operating profit to 129.4 million in the year to end-September.
"This was below our expectations because most of the growth in television advertising in calendar 1996 will fall into the first quarter of our current financial year," she added.

Carlton said there was modest growth in advertising revenue in the second half of its financial year. Its airtime is sold by its Carlton Sales unit, whose income represents 22 percent of total UK television advertising revenue.

Operating profit at Carlton's Video division grew by 21 percent to 73.2 million stg. The division, which produces and distributes pre-recorded videocassettes, benefited from the sustained growth of the video sell-through market.
Carlton Home Entertainment, part of the Video division, reduced its operating losses although the company said they remained high relative to sales.

Carlton Home Entertainment, formerly known as Pickwick, publishes and distributes a range of video and budget music titles. The company is expecting it to show a significant improvement in the current year.

Carlton said it was preparing for the introduction of Digital Video Disc (DVD) players and will produce DVDs at its Technicolor Optical Media plant in California. The players were launched in Japan last month and are expected to be introduced in the U.S. in the first half of next year.
Operating profits at Carlton's Film division grew by 27 percent to 52.7 million stg.
The division processes motion picture film and has gained from major studios' policy of releasing their films to large numbers of cinemas at one time.
Carlton said that its customers released five films to over 3,000 screens per movie in the month of June alone.
"We fully expect this pattern of release to endure, though it is unlikely that future rates of growth can match recent experience," Moller said.

Operating profit from the company's Products division rose to 43.1 million stg from 32.5 million. Carlton said it was on course to become leader in tapeless editing for the worldwide television industry.
